source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
method: Additive verbatim-provenance-linked paraphrase. No species JSON or photos changed. Only source-extracted species counted.

morphology.habit: Nearly leafless rhizomatous perennial forming clumps, rushlike
morphology.stems: Glabrous/glabrate, glaucous photosynthetic erect, 0.5–1.5(–2.5) m, freely branched, lasting up to about four growing seasons
morphology.spines: Some branchlets become thorns 10–20 mm long
morphology.rays: Approximately 10–33 white, sometimes bluish, ligules ≤5.5 mm

diagnostic_or_conflict_notes: Distinctive nearly leafless photosynthetic stems; could be mistaken for a rush in habit.

morphology.habit: Coarse winter annual or biennial, flowers from ~25 cm to 2 m
morphology.foliage: Green on both surfaces, thinly pubescent to glabrous, spiny-margined
morphology.heads: Usually solitary terminal heads; involucres wider than long, 4–8 cm broad
morphology.false_involucre: Approximately 10–12 prominently spiny leafy bracts directly under involucre
morphology.florets: Only disk florets, rosy-lavender; rarely yellow in southeast Texas
morphology.pappus: Plumose bristles united at base, per genus
morphology.habitat: Damp open woods and lowland sites

diagnostic_or_conflict_notes: Regional author called this bull thistle, but also uses that common name for introduced C. vulgare: scientific characters avoid common-name ambiguity.
Regional flora's 4–8 cm figure is involucre width, not height.

morphology.habit: Strongly spiny biennial or perennial 0.2–1(–1.5) m
morphology.foliage: Whitish tomentose below; upper grayish woolly and usually somewhat darker
morphology.leaf_attachment: Uniformly deep-pinnatifid mid/upper leaves, decurrent into spiny stem wings >1 cm in 1999 flora key
morphology.heads: Oblong involucres 2.5–4.5 cm high per key, initially taller than broad
morphology.phyllaries: Mid/outer tips (5–)7–15 mm long per key
morphology.florets: Rosy lavender/purple, rarely white, disk only

diagnostic_or_conflict_notes: Leaf-wing and phyllary spine contrasts versus C. undulatum are tendencies in this regional key; FNA may vary geographically.

morphology.foliage: Upper green glabrous to lightly tomentose; undersides thinly grayish/whitish tomentose; upper sessile and slightly clasping
morphology.heads: Involucres relatively small, 1.4–2.2 cm tall, approximately as wide as tall when flowering; no false leafy spiny basal whorl
morphology.florets: Pink to deep rosy-lavender disk flowers; no true ray

diagnostic_or_conflict_notes: Regional 0.5–2 m stature wider than existing learner simplification 'under about 1m'; preserve broad source measurement.
Upper stem wings can occur; do not use wing presence alone to diagnose introduced thistles.

morphology.foliage: Leaves can be nearly as tomentose above as below; leaf edges sometimes wavy, generally shallowly pinnatifid per key
morphology.stem_attachment: Clasping, decurrent by ≤1 cm or not decurrent in 1999 flora key
morphology.heads: Involucres 2.5–4.5 cm high, oblong/urnlike, longer than broad while flowering
morphology.phyllaries: Prickle tips of mid/outer phyllaries 1–5 mm

diagnostic_or_conflict_notes: Wavy leaf margins variable, not diagnostic on their own.
Compare C. ochrocentrum phyllary spine lengths and leaf dissection; account for overlap.

morphology.foliage: Upper blade with numerous short yellowish appressed prickles, distinct from long marginal spines; green upper surface, sometimes gray pubescent underside
morphology.stem_attachment: Decurrent spiny leaf bases form wings

diagnostic_or_conflict_notes: 1999 flora documents early Texas invasion history; historic date is not current abundance.
Leaf-surface prickles, not just winged stems, are emphasized by the regional diagnostic key.

morphology.heads: Corymbose clusters of disk-only blue/purplish-blue florets; no rays
morphology.fruits: 5-ribbed dark cypselae with bristle pappus per broad Eupatorium generic account
morphology.habitat: Moist often wooded sandy or calcareous places

diagnostic_or_conflict_notes: 1999 flora explicitly mentions transfer to Conoclinium; no concept conflict in this account.
